dialog.title: Let agents publish on their own?

points.what: Agents you allow will publish new pages to Webflow, WordPress and Wix, send drafts to your CMS and send pages to your webhook, without anyone clicking.
points.responsible: Your workspace is responsible for what they publish, as if a member had clicked Publish.
points.limits: Each agent needs its own permission from an Admin, runs in Full auto, and goes live at most its daily limit (5 unless an Admin changes it).
points.checks: Before a page goes out, it must pass Quality and match your approved brand facts. If it doesn't, or if the run read text that tried to instruct it, it waits for a click.
points.told: You get an Inbox notice for each one. Pages on WordPress, Webflow and Wix can be taken down in one click. Webhook sends can't be taken back.

citation-winback.name: Citation Win-back

competitor-watch.name: Competitor Watch

content-freshness.name: Content Freshness
content-freshness.description: Finds cited pages with old dates, numbers or examples and drafts the update.

ready-to-publish.name: Ready to Publish
ready-to-publish.description: Runs a quality pass on a draft, fills its page fields, sends a CMS draft and publishes it. It goes live on its own only if an Admin allows it.

task-finisher.name: Task Finisher
task-finisher.description: Works through this week’s Action Center tasks by priority and prepares each one. You close the tasks.

weekly-report.name: Weekly Report
weekly-report.description: Your week in AI answers on one page: citations, mentions and share of voice, what changed and why.

brand-facts-guardian.name: Brand Facts Guardian
brand-facts-guardian.description: Finds AI answers that get facts about your brand wrong and drafts the fixes against your brand facts.

fanout-gap-filler.name: Fan-out Gap Filler
fanout-gap-filler.description: Drafts answer-first sections for the sub-questions AI searches where your brand is missing.

prompt-portfolio.name: Prompt Portfolio Manager
prompt-portfolio.description: Proposes prompts to add and to pause, so tracking stays on what matters.

onboarding-help.name: Onboarding & Help
onboarding-help.description: Answers questions about GetCito from Help and walks new members through setup.

shopping-readiness.name: AI Shopping Readiness
shopping-readiness.description: Checks product pages and the feed when the catalog syncs, and drafts the fixes.

localization.name: Localization
localization.description: When a page goes live in your main language, drafts it for your other markets.

aeo-operator.name: AEO Operator
aeo-operator.description: Each morning, picks which agents to run within a budget and sends you one summary to approve.

technical-fixer.name: Crawler & Technical Fixer
technical-fixer.description: Fixes what keeps AI crawlers out and sends the fix to your site’s code as a pull request.

third-party-sources.name: Third-party Sources
third-party-sources.description: Finds the threads, videos and review pages AI cites where you’re missing, and plans outreach.

revenue-attribution.name: Revenue Attribution
revenue-attribution.description: Each week, the contacts, deals and revenue AI answers brought, by engine and page.

ticket-loop.name: Ticket Loop
ticket-loop.description: Sends Action Center tasks to Jira or Linear, follows them and adds the measured result.

agency-reporter.name: Agency Client Reporter
agency-reporter.description: A monthly report for each client brand, for agencies.

ai-ads-watch.name: AI Ads Watch
ai-ads-watch.description: Shows who advertises inside AI answers on your prompts, and where.

product-answer-pages.name: Product Answer Pages
product-answer-pages.description: Finds the “best X for Y” questions buyers ask AI and drafts answer-first product copy and comparison tables.

shopping-feed-advisor.name: Shopping Feed Advisor
shopping-feed-advisor.description: Finds the product attributes your feed lacks for AI shopping and prepares the fixes for your feed.

seasonal-prompt-planner.name: Seasonal Prompt Planner
seasonal-prompt-planner.description: Before peaks such as Black Friday or back-to-school, proposes the prompts to track and the pages to prepare.

app-store-listing.name: App Store Listing for AI
app-store-listing.description: Checks the app store pages AI cites for “best app for…” questions and drafts changes to your listing.

app-alternatives-watch.name: App Alternatives Watch
app-alternatives-watch.description: Finds where AI lists rival apps instead of yours, and the store pages behind it.

feature-question-coverage.name: Feature-question Coverage
feature-question-coverage.description: Finds the features AI credits to rivals but not to you, and drafts help answers to “can it do…” questions.

alternatives-comparison-pages.name: Alternatives & Comparison Pages
alternatives-comparison-pages.description: Drafts “X vs Y” and alternatives pages, then checks them against how AI compares you, feature by feature.

review-site-presence.name: Review-site Presence
review-site-presence.description: Checks the review sites AI cites in your category, how they show you, and the profile tasks to do. It never posts.

integration-questions.name: Integration Questions
integration-questions.description: Finds the “does it work with…” questions buyers ask AI and drafts answers for your docs and integration pages.

reviews-ugc-watch.name: Reviews & UGC Watch
reviews-ugc-watch.description: Watches the review sites and communities AI cites about you and plans what to answer. It never posts.

local-store-locator.name: Local & Store Locator
local-store-locator.description: Checks the local listings and store pages AI uses for “near me” questions.

social-proof-pages.name: Social-proof Pages
social-proof-pages.description: Drafts the FAQ answers AI quotes on returns, shipping and guarantees, checked against your brand facts.

content-plan-builder.name: Content Plan Builder
content-plan-builder.description: Each week, turns content opportunities into a plan and a brief for each page.

narrative-sentiment-watch.name: Narrative & Sentiment Watch
narrative-sentiment-watch.description: How AI describes your brand on each engine, in its own words, and the wrong claims to fix.

source-outreach-list.name: Source Outreach List
source-outreach-list.description: Lists the publications and directories AI cites for your topics, whether each lists you, and the next step. It never sends.

ceo-brief.name: CEO Brief
ceo-brief.description: Each Monday, one page for leaders: whether AI recommends you more, what moved, and where to win next.

ai-traffic-signups.name: AI Traffic → Signups
ai-traffic-signups.description: Shows the prompts and pages that bring AI visitors who sign up.

market-source-finder.name: Market & Source Finder

cloudflare_worker.name: Cloudflare Worker
cloudflare_worker.what: A small Worker on your site's route passes every request through and sends only AI-bot requests, in batches.
cloudflare_worker.cost: On your Cloudflare bill: free up to 100,000 requests a day, then $5 a month for 10 million and $0.30 per extra million. It runs on every request, so busy sites may need the paid plan.

cloudflare_logpush.name: Cloudflare Logpush
cloudflare_logpush.what: Cloudflare sends only the log lines of AI bots, filtered at its edge. Nothing runs on your requests.
cloudflare_logpush.cost: Logpush is on all Cloudflare plans and avoids the per-request Worker cost; whether the HTTP requests dataset is available depends on your account.

vercel_drain.name: Vercel Drain
vercel_drain.what: Vercel sends your request logs; GetCito keeps the AI bots and drops the rest.
vercel_drain.cost: Vercel Pro and Enterprise only, at $0.50 per GB of drained data on your Vercel bill.

cloudflare_worker: In Cloudflare, open Workers & Pages and create a Worker.
Replace its code with the Worker code below and deploy it.
In the Worker's Settings › Variables and Secrets, add a variable of type Secret with the name and value below.
Add a route for your site, such as example.com/*, so the Worker sees its requests.
cloudflare_logpush: In Cloudflare, open Analytics & Logs › Logpush and create a job for the HTTP requests dataset.
Choose HTTP destination and paste the destination below.
Pick the fields and the filter from the job settings below, or create the job through the API with them.
vercel_drain: In Vercel, open Team Settings › Drains and add a Logs drain for your site's project.
Choose Custom endpoint and paste the endpoint URL below.
Set the format to JSON and add the custom header below.

consent.label: Consent
consent.always: Don't wait: our own banner covers it
consent.waitHint: No id is kept and no journey is sent until your site says the visitor agreed. AI visits themselves are counted as before.
consent.alwaysHint: Use this only if your cookie banner already asks for analytics storage, or where no consent is needed.

steps.tagHelp: It replaces the tag you have, before the closing {tag} tag of every page. The first line lets your site call getcito() before the tag has loaded.
steps.consentHelp: Call this from your cookie banner once the visitor agrees, and on every page after.
steps.denyHelp: Call this when the visitor says no, or takes consent back, and on every page after, while they say no: the id kept in their browser is deleted, and nothing more is sent.
steps.consentMode: Google Consent Mode works on its own: the snippet follows {name}. A banner set up inside Google Tag Manager needs a tag for each line above, run when the visitor chooses.
steps.formsHelp: A form with an email field counts as a signup, contact and newsletter forms too: add {goal} to name its goal (demo, newsletter, booking), or {off} to leave it out. A login with a password doesn't count. Don't also call a signup from your own code for the same form, or it counts twice.
steps.callsHelp: Call these from your own code, on a thank-you page or after a purchase. The tag's first line keeps them until it loads.
steps.shopifyHelp: In Shopify admin, open Settings › Customer events › Add custom pixel and name it GetCito. Under Customer privacy, set Permission to Analytics and Data sale to "Data collected does not qualify as data sale". Paste this code, save, then connect it.
steps.shopifyConsent: Your store asks for consent: add this to your theme (theme.liquid, after the tag) so Shopify's cookie banner gives its answer.
steps.shopifyHeadless: A headless store whose checkout is on another domain can't link its orders this way.
